DM: I mean he's like you know clearly a, you know, a somewhat experienced soldier. Not obvious that he's seen a lot of combat. He's not as old as—he's not like in his 60s. He's probably in his late 30s, early 40s, um, but he's well built, wearing armor.
DM: You can see that the he's not wearing any jewelry. There's no rings on his fingers um.
DM: And ah, is he has a sword like like out, and he’s sort of like pacing with a sword slung over his shoulder like this, um.
DM: Turns as you enter. Where are the rest of them?

Kenzo: They’re still outside. Kenzo says, they're still outside, but Illyan, first allow me to apologize for the use of magic in your space, and it was—I think the valet may have already communicated this, but it was a member of our party, that was a member of our party that that was trying to investigate ahead to see if there were any traps, again we apologize for the use of magic in this way, but I hope you'll appreciate over the past several months being out at the frontiers and Karawa and facing the myriad dangers that we've had to deal with. Gnolls, warlocks, all kinds of stuff with, you know, creatures with strange magic. Um, it's been an incredibly stressful and dangerous time, so.
DM: He waves it down and points it, like slightly cutting you off, points it at you and says, “You should know that spying on a military command is a capital offense.”
DM: Right, he then turns his sword and like puts it down in the ground.
DM: But I will not threaten you now.
DM: For we have a more pressing matter from the gods to deal with.
Kenzo: How can we be of service, or how can I be of service?
DM: What do you know of the Nayan Sura?
Kenzo: Nayan Sura is the, the—
Kenzo: What, what do you know of Nayan Sura?
DM: I'm asking the questions here. You're on thin ice, as it is.
Kenzo: Tim, I Soul Sight him.
DM: Upset like but also like you do get the sense like he is genuinely feels driven by a mission from the gods.
Kenzo: Okay okay. Um, Nayan Sura. Well, have you spoken with Kaleha about this topic? Because I shared some information with Kaleha about Nayan Sura.
DM: It is on her behalf, but I am speaking to you now.
Kenzo: Okay, in that case, then what I have shared with Kaleha, and I can reshare again to you what I shared with her, but that is what I know.
Kenzo: We were, I was completely transparent. We were completely transparent in our conversation with, with her.
DM: Is she set on a battle?
Kenzo: Of that I have no idea. I do not know.
Wellby: Assuming he’s meaning is Nayan Sura.
DM: What does she want? Do you know?

Kenzo: These are excellent questions, and I share with you in utmost sincerity as a Dunmari myself and my companions, our greatest wish is to avoid bloodshed. Our greatest wish is for the Dunmari people to achieve peace, to thrive in harmony.
Kenzo: Obviously the appearance of Nayan Sura is not a an event that is without political consequence, of course. I'm not foolish enough to, to see otherwise, but.

Kenzo: In my brief interactions and in seeing her in Karawa it's not clear to me what her goal or motivation is, but I can share with you that my and my companions goal is to try to achieve peace and is to try to avoid bloodshed at all costs.
DM: You are an initiate, are you not?
Kenzo: I am indeed. Honor-bound to the gods.
DM: What did you see in her soul?
DM: At least that’s good news. And you have no idea who did this to her?
Kenzo: As I shared with Kaleha, we found her trapped inside, inside one of his traps, and so who trapped her, what dealings that person or persons may have had with Agata is, is unknown to us.
Wellby: Quick point of order, we think it was Agata's henchman who, who did the abduction, but we don’t know—
Wellby: On whose behalf, he did that.
DM: Do you know where she is now?
Kenzo: Right now I do not. When we left Karawa, she was still there in the city.
Kenzo: What has happened since then we do not know.
DM: Do you think she would listen to you? Is there anyone she would listen to? We needed to get her a message.

Kenzo: Kenzo laughs. It's funny, I've tried my whole life to stay out of Dunmar politics. I hate to volunteer myself and my companions, but I think she would be likely to listen to us given our role in helping to free her.
Kenzo: Is there a message you'd like, I'd like for us to, to pass on?
DM: Looking at you, he says: Kaleha left it to my judgment after I met you how much to say. I will admit there is a part of me that is skeptical. Your spying, your companions’—
DM: Cowardice clinging to their weapons and whatever else they might possess and refusing to even speak with me does not put you in a good light. Well, does not put them in a good light.
DM: Little faith in them. But I can see the gods cling to you Kenzo.

DM: So I will share this. Kaleha told me she prayed all night asking Sonkar what was to be done. And the only answer she received was vision after vision after vision of death, of people being split in two and a sense of dread.
DM: Whatever the gods wish for Dunmar, they do not wish us to fight. That much is clear.
DM: And so now I'm tasked with how to stop a war—don't even, not even know that anybody wants.
DM: Except that wars often happen by accident without anyone meaning it just by the force of events and destiny.
DM: So I would ask that this message get to Sura. The political future of Dunmar must be in the hands of the gods.
DM: To give us time to understand their purpose, she must not bring an army west of the Hara, and we will not cross the river east.

Kenzo: That's a very fair position. Can I ask, then, and if you are entrusting us to deliver this message, I think that’s a task that I certainly would be willing to take, and I’m guessing my companions would as well, but do you know—what—what's the name of the king?
Kenzo: Do you know what Karnas means to do?

DM: He’s far. Messages are slow. He is aware. Magic lets us speak, but only briefly. Plan—yes. Many are suspicious of a woman who was a prisoner of a hag for eight years. A hag known to have—well, a hag known to despise Dunmar and have a desire for misery at her heart. There's little good that can come of that.

Kenzo: I understand that concern, but again as amongst the party that freed her she seemed as though the magic of her of where she was trapped—she didn't have a memory of being trapped for eight years, so.
Kenzo: Again, from my own, my own examination of her, she seems to be untainted and un-, un- affected by, by Agata. Now, that said.
Kenzo: I think it's a great political consequence, the question of who put her in the trap, who collaborated with Agata to ensnare her. This we do not know, and this is of great and dire consequence.
Kenzo: And so, one thing really I ask you as a fellow Dunmari, and again I appreciate and understand your, your suspicions, and I apologize again for getting off on the wrong foot with you here, but.
Kenzo: Can I ask what the Chardonians are doing here?
DM: Wow that is common knowledge that there has been disruptions of a magical nature to the east and one should not go to fight magic without magic at your back.
DM: I will say no more.
DM: And I agree. It is—how this chain of events started seems of deep political importance.
Kenzo: When I'm Sighting Illyan when he's talking about the Chardonians, is he like they're awesome? Is he, like like you know.
Kenzo: Like is he, like, if you like, this is a relationship of convenience, am I scared of them, am I, you know um what's his vibe?
DM: So with 18, I mean his vibe is kind of you know, he was ordered to work with these people.

DM: But also like there is a bit of a genuine like he doesn't know what's out there. There’s not that many of them, but they’re pretty strong and, like, obviously they’re useful, like—right, you saw them being useful right so there's.
DM: There's a bit of I was ordered to work with them I you know I think I get along with them, but actually they turned out to be great group members right like that.
Kenzo: Okay. So, Illyan, would you like us to pass this message on to find Sura and pass this message on to them?
DM: If you know where to find her I would greatly appreciate that. That would go a long way to making up for the questionable actions of your companions.
Kenzo: Again I share in that responsibility so any, any—yeah, so don’t, don’t, please don’t, don’t, don’t slap them.
Kenzo: On the road, I was, I was a part of that decision as well.

Kenzo: Okay. This is something that we can—all I'll discuss with my companions. There's also a scroll of Sending, that’s interesting. That's very interesting. Yeah. Is there any other, anything else you’d like to discuss for the moment?
DM: That is all, and I thank you.

Kenzo: And Illyan again my deepest apologies for for our transgression, but I hope you also understand our caution and my caution, given the events that have unfolded, given the dealings, even with the gods on our side.
Kenzo: But I appreciate greatly your your your sharing of, of what you know, and let me discuss with my companions how best we can, we can get the message to Sura.
DM: He sort of nods and says, I— if it was anyone else your head would be on the floor. Those who killed Agata. I imagine dealing with a creature such as her must induce quite a bunch of paranoia.
Kenzo: You have no idea. Dealing with a witch like that, nothing is what it seems. No message seems what it's what it should be. No doorway, no entry way seems what it means what it should be—
DM: When did it occur with just her messing with us.
Kenzo: There is no paranoia that is too extreme when talking about her given our experience.
DM: The—confer with your companions. Let me know when you're ready to leave.

before: DM: It's not you can't see an aura, but you can sense the presence of magic right right.
Kenzo: So Kenzo literally just takes off—

DM: Like you're like you're stopped like about 30 feet from the entrance to the tent is where the—and as he puts some stuff down you know, Drusa walks with you, yeah, perfect, and as soon as she gets to the entrance of the tent, she nods to the valet, like he’s clear, like once she’s about 35 feet away from the pile of stuff and the rest of you.
DM: And motions you forward and it's on you. You talk to them.
Kenzo: I will. Thank you.
after: Kenzo: I shall step outside. Look around to the guards. Mind if we have a moment, companions?
Unknown: Yeah they'll a little little.
Kenzo: Share what what what happened.
Wellby: I feel like this is kind of a best case scenario.
Seeker: You really saved us there, Kenzo, thanks.

interactions.title: Illyan approves a Sending message and safe conduct
lines: Kenzo: This is a good message here, friends. I’ll share this draft with—so explain to Illyan, Illyan, you know, we have this, we have the ability to send a message with Sending scrolls, be like—I think that they would know about.
Kenzo: I explain it, explain to him that we have the scroll, that we can actually reach out to her right away. This is the message we propose to send. What do you think?
DM: That's gonna save you a lot of riding if it works.
Kenzo: Do you approve this message?
DM: Yeah he's fine with that.

Kenzo: And you also agree on because again will will close will conclude the message with them sending a messenger as well, so that a more direct communication can be, a direct, a more direct communication can be held between, between your parties.
DM: That would be ideal, even if only to help make sure the truce can hold and figure out how to discern the gods' will.
Wellby: Can he promise safe conduct? That could be our last two words.
DM: I can promise safe conduct for a messenger, not for her.

before: DM: No, well, you could, but it would take some time. It would take several days, many days.
Seeker: Days.
Unknown: Okay.
Kenzo: Got two more words—
Wellby: Love us.
after: Seeker: Nice.
Kenzo: Alright, so let me, let me put down the full thing—
Seeker: I had a funny moment where I copy pasted it thinking okay now you just need to, and I can just paste it into the scroll sending.
Seeker: Like instant messengers.
Kenzo: That'd be cool. So let me copy it, but you guys oh that's why the fuck.

interactions.title: Sura replies that she will not fight
lines: DM: So Seeker takes out the scroll.
DM: And you begin casting and the scroll begins to burn up. And, as it burns to ash it blows away and you speak this message, willing it to reach Sura’s ears.
DM: And for a long time there's silence. And then you hear back: “I also wish to know gods’ will. I do not know how their will will be known. But until then, I will not fight.”
Kenzo: But, but, did she say anything about sending a messenger?
Seeker: She might do that, didn’t mention.
DM: You know you don't know whether she will send a messenger.
Kenzo: Wait wait so, Tim, how do we know that, how do we know that they got the message back? Like, what’s the—do we get something written back from them, or—?
DM: He hears it in his head.
Seeker: Okay, so I write it down quickly so that we can—

before: Kenzo: Alright if he approves Tim let's let's send the shit.
Wellby: Should be “Illyan offers truce.”
Delwath: I would actually move the “offers truce” up to after Kaleha because ultimately it's—

Kenzo: You know, Illyan, I'm guessing Kaleha knows this as well, but when the Lakan monks return to the monastery, you will have the ability to communicate with her again. At least one of the monks in the monastery is able to produce the same type of magic we used to communicate with her just now. So when the monks return, I'm sure you or Kaleha—it'd be wise for you to contact the monastery and if you wish to send an additional communiqué, I’m sure you could do so then.
DM: Indeed, Kaleha deeply desires the guidance of Lara now. And I'm sure they will speak when she returns.
Kenzo: Then, Illyan, I’m grateful that we could be of service and that this message was communicated to Sura. I honestly am tremendously relieved to hear your and Kaleha’s position.
